# HHeatmap

> Keyboard-inspectable numeric matrices with missing-data cells and a shared intensity scale.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HHeatmap` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-heatmap>`.
- Constructor: `HearthHeatmapElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HHeatmap.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Rows and columns follow first appearance in cells. Missing/nonfinite values show No data, distinct from zero. Cells use native table headers and named buttons with arrow/Home/End navigation; select emits a cell ID. The shared intensity scale uses min/max when provided. Default limits are 32 rows and 64 columns, each configurable up to 128; omitted axes are disclosed.

## Public API

cells: HeatmapCell[] · label, unit: string · min, max, maxRows, maxColumns: number · tone: Tone · selected: string

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label: string;
    cells: HeatmapCell[];
    unit?: string;
    tone?: Tone;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    maxRows?: number;
    maxColumns?: number;
    selected?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ cells: () => [], unit: "", tone: "accent", maxRows: 32, maxColumns: 64 }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, cell

Use `hearth-heatmap::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface HeatmapCell {
    id: string;
    row: string;
    column: string;
    value: number | null;
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HHeatmap } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HHeatmap label="Request activity" :cells="[{id:'a',row:'API',column:'09:00',value:12},{id:'b',row:'API',column:'10:00',value:28},{id:'c',row:'Worker',column:'09:00',value:6},{id:'d',row:'Worker',column:'10:00',value:null}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-heatmap');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Request activity",
  "cells": [
    {
      "id": "a",
      "row": "API",
      "column": "09:00",
      "value": 12
    },
    {
      "id": "b",
      "row": "API",
      "column": "10:00",
      "value": 28
    },
    {
      "id": "c",
      "row": "Worker",
      "column": "09:00",
      "value": 6
    },
    {
      "id": "d",
      "row": "Worker",
      "column": "10:00",
      "value": null
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
